leads.title: Bearcreek Farms, Inc. v. S.L.S. Partnership
leads.court: Ohio Court of Appeals, Second District (Montgomery County)
leads.why: Published Nov. 25, 2026 opinion (C.A. No. 30820). Bearcreek Farms, Inc. (buyer) sued seller S.L.S. Partnership and its partners, plus tenant Jacqueline S. Ritter, Inc. d/b/a Laffs Pub (JSR), over ownership of fixtures (a commercial bar, freezer, steel kitchen hood) at 2 E. Center Street, Germantown, Ohio, after Bearcreek bought the building under a purchase agreement conveying 'all buildings, improvements and fixtures.' The trial court dismissed Bearcreek's breach-of-contract and general-warranty-deed claims under Civ.R. 12(B)(6); the Second District reversed and remanded, holding the complaint stated a claim that the fixtures were conveyed and that JSR's competing ownership claim could breach the deed's warranty covenants. Primary source is the opinion itself (CourtListener); no secondary press coverage found. Commercial real estate purchase/fixtures dispute between businesses -- parties are Bearcreek Farms Inc., S.L.S. Partnership, and JSR Inc., no individuals need be named.

leads.title: Karen Lodzinski v. Fieldspring Investments, LLC
leads.court: New Jersey Superior Court, Appellate Division
leads.why: Approved-for-publication opinion issued Nov. 25, 2026 (Docket A-3971-24), a case of first impression: the Appellate Division held the NJ Law Against Discrimination can, in appropriate circumstances, protect a commercial tenant from a landlord's severe or pervasive sexual harassment, vacating the trial court's pre-answer dismissal of plaintiff's suit against landlord Fieldspring Investments, LLC (and individual co-defendant). This is a commercial-landlord-liability precedent of real interest to owners/landlords, though the named plaintiff and the co-defendant are individuals -- if published, name only the business party (Fieldspring Investments, LLC), consistent with the no-individuals rule. Primary source is the opinion; no secondary press coverage found yet.

leads.title: 28 investors v. Sotheby's International Realty Affiliates, LLC (The Ascent, Park City, Utah condo-hotel)
leads.court: U.S. District Court, Central District of California
leads.why: 28 investors sued Sotheby's International Realty Affiliates, LLC in C.D. Cal. (filed Oct. 9, 2026 per KPCW/mpamag), alleging the brokerage marketed condo-hotel units at The Ascent near Canyons Village, Park City, Utah as safe, Hilton-affiliated investments without disclosing that developer T S 1, LLC lacked the money to finish construction. The project was later foreclosed: lender OKOA won an August 2026 trustee's auction with a $24M bid, wiping out the investors' interests per the complaint. Reported by KPCW and Salt Lake Tribune on Nov. 16, also mpamag and unofficialnetworks. Flagging for the geographic-diversity goal -- Utah currently has only 2 tracked matters -- even though the filing (Oct. 9) and first reporting found (Nov. 16) are both a bit outside the preferred 3/7-day windows; newsroom should judge freshness (first-public-date rule) and pull the actual complaint/docket number before publishing.
